claims.proposition: An average causal effect contrasts expected outcomes under two specified interventions in a specified population; for a binary outcome a risk difference is expressed in probability or percentage points.

A valid adjustment formula combines conditional outcome distributions with the same pre-intervention covariate distribution for each treatment. Validity depends on the causal structure, not merely on including many variables.

resources.text: People who choose a programme may differ before it begins. What exactly would change if the same eligible population were assigned the programme instead?
Worked example

Consider students eligible for a six-week study-support programme. Define A=1 as assignment to the scheduled study-support programme and A=0 as assignment to the stated comparison programme. Define the outcome as passing the declared skills check at six weeks. Fix the eligibility rule, follow-up time and programme version, so 'the effect' refers to one clear decision.

Looking only at people who selected A=1 keeps their original selection process. Motivation, access and baseline learning difficulty may explain both selection and the later outcome. An intervention instead specifies a rule for setting A; it does not merely filter existing rows.

A trial could randomize programme assignment while measuring the same endpoint in both arms. This directly addresses assignment to the specified programmes under the trial conditions. It does not automatically identify the effect of attendance when people do not follow assignment, nor effects of an unspecified future programme.

An intervention changes how a treatment variable is set. do(A=1) denotes setting A to 1 in the model; observing A=1 denotes selecting cases whose existing value is 1. The two distributions can differ.
A before/after comparison or a group of enthusiastic volunteers is not automatically equivalent to random assignment. The source of treatment differences matters.
Write the treatment, comparison, eligible population, endpoint and timing before asking which records can answer the question.
Random assignment sets the reminder under a declared rule. Filtering existing reminder users retains self-selection; a historical comparison also changes time and potentially the population.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. Random assignment sets the reminder under a declared rule. Filtering existing reminder users retains self-selection; a historical comparison also changes time and potentially the population.
Ask whether the plan changes the assignment rule or only selects existing records.

A library wants the effect of assigning a return-date reminder on on-time returns next month. It currently has records of readers who switched reminders on themselves. Which additional plan directly changes assignment?
Random assignment sets the reminder under a declared rule. Filtering existing reminder users retains self-selection; a historical comparison also changes time and potentially the population.
The assignment intervention is the offer. An effect of actual use is a different target because uptake can be selective; transporting any result to a new policy or population needs further support.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. The assignment intervention is the offer. An effect of actual use is a different target because uptake can be selective; transporting any result to a new policy or population needs further support.
The randomized variable is the offer, not later uptake.

A college randomly offers a travel voucher, but some offered students do not use it. The endpoint is attendance within 30 days. Which intervention contrast does comparing the randomized groups directly target?
The assignment intervention is the offer. An effect of actual use is a different target because uptake can be selective; transporting any result to a new policy or population needs further support.
Suppose the target population's mean outcome would be 68 skills-score points under programme A and 62 under programme B. What does the difference describe?
Worked example

The contrast describes two alternative assignments for the same target population, not the difference between whichever people happened to choose A and whichever chose B. The two expected outcomes are defined before choosing an estimator.

For the continuous score, A minus B is 68 - 62 = +6 skills-score points. If the outcome were whether a target was reached, a change from 60% to 75% would be +15 percentage points. That differs from a relative increase of 25%. State which quantity you report.

A positive average contrast need not mean that every person benefits. Some may benefit more, some less and some may be harmed. A finite study estimates the population contrast with uncertainty; the arithmetic alone is not an uncertainty analysis.
The average treatment effect is E[Y under do(A=1)] - E[Y under do(A=0)] for a stated population and outcome. Direction, units, timing and assignment versions are part of its meaning.
Do not turn a percentage-point difference into a relative percentage or an individual guarantee. Changing the population mixture can also change an average effect.
Report the two expected outcomes, their difference and its units, then name the target population.
68 - 62 = +6 skills-score points. This is a group-average estimate in the declared study, not each person's effect or a 6% relative change.
Reconsider the distinction in this case. 68 - 62 = +6 skills-score points. This is a group-average estimate in the declared study, not each person's effect or a 6% relative change.
Subtract B from A and keep the outcome's original units.

In a randomized teaching dataset of eligible learners, the mean six-week skills score is 68 under A and 62 under B. Ignoring sampling uncertainty for this arithmetic question, what is the A-minus-B contrast?
68 - 62 = +6 skills-score points. This is a group-average estimate in the declared study, not each person's effect or a 6% relative change.
0.54 - 0.40 = 0.14, or 14 percentage points. The relative increase is 0.14/0.40 = 35%; the data do not identify the response of each individual.
Reconsider the distinction in this case. 0.54 - 0.40 = 0.14, or 14 percentage points. The relative increase is 0.14/0.40 = 35%; the data do not identify the response of each individual.
Compute the difference between probabilities; a relative change divides that difference by the comparison risk.
A randomized follow-up dataset reports course completion in 54 of 100 assigned A and 40 of 100 assigned B by day 30. Which statement reports the risk difference correctly?
0.54 - 0.40 = 0.14, or 14 percentage points. The relative increase is 0.14/0.40 = 35%; the data do not identify the response of each individual.
What if people with higher baseline learning difficulty more often choose the intensive programme and also have lower success regardless of programme?
Worked example

If baseline learning difficulty affects programme choice and the outcome, the raw A and B groups mix different starting conditions. Comparing their overall success rates can combine the programme contrast with this compositional difference.

Imagine success rates of 80% versus 70% in the lower difficulty stratum and 50% versus 40% in the higher difficulty stratum. In a target population that is half in each stratum, standardize A to 0.5×80% + 0.5×50% = 65%, and B to 0.5×70% + 0.5×40% = 55%. Both use the target mixture, giving +10 percentage points.

The calculation has a causal interpretation only if the selected pre-treatment strata suffice to control confounding, both treatments are possible in each relevant stratum, and the treatment/outcome definitions are consistent. Adding every measured variable is unsafe: a mediator changes the target and conditioning on a collider can introduce bias.

Covariate adjustment estimates each treatment's outcome within valid pre-treatment strata and averages using the same target-population distribution. A valid adjustment set is a causal assumption, not a property guaranteed by a spreadsheet.
Different weights for A and B reproduce selection rather than remove it. A weighted calculation cannot fix a missing common cause or a stratum with no comparison cases.
Name why the adjustment set is valid, check overlap, then apply one declared target mixture to both treatment-specific rates.

With an adequate pre-treatment adjustment set and overlap, one common target mixture separates treatment-specific rates from differences in who selected each treatment. These assumptions, not the number of columns, license the calculation.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. With an adequate pre-treatment adjustment set and overlap, one common target mixture separates treatment-specific rates from differences in who selected each treatment. These assumptions, not the number of columns, license the calculation.
The two hypothetical assignments must refer to the same target population.

Baseline workload affects both support-programme choice and task completion. Under the stated model it is the only common cause, both programmes occur at each workload and versions are consistent. How should a target-population effect be calculated?

With an adequate pre-treatment adjustment set and overlap, one common target mixture separates treatment-specific rates from differences in who selected each treatment. These assumptions, not the number of columns, license the calculation.

The declared baseline set is adequate here. Adjusting for a mediator would generally target a different contrast, and other structures such as colliders can create bias. Neither maximal adjustment nor a blanket rejection of observational inference follows.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. The declared baseline set is adequate here. Adjusting for a mediator would generally target a different contrast, and other structures such as colliders can create bias. Neither maximal adjustment nor a blanket rejection of observational inference follows.
A variable measured after treatment may lie on a pathway through which treatment works.

A learning-platform registry records baseline preparation and later study time. The goal is the total effect of coaching on passing. Assume baseline preparation is an adequate adjustment set. A colleague adds later study time because it predicts passing. What is the sound response?

The declared baseline set is adequate here. Adjusting for a mediator would generally target a different contrast, and other structures such as colliders can create bias. Neither maximal adjustment nor a blanket rejection of observational inference follows.
If two causal explanations fit the same recorded association but disagree about a deliberate change, can the records choose between their effects?
Worked example

The intervention effect is the target quantity. Identification asks whether the observed distribution and accepted assumptions determine that quantity. Estimation asks how accurately a finite sample approximates the identified expression. More data reduce sampling uncertainty but do not resolve an unacknowledged causal ambiguity.

For students eligible for a six-week study-support programme, adjustment by baseline learning difficulty requires that no additional common cause remains after conditioning on it, that both programmes are available in relevant strata, and that the specified treatment corresponds to observed versions. Random assignment can support a different identification argument for assignment effects when follow-up and implementation are adequate.

Even a sound within-study identification argument does not establish transport to a new population, a new programme version or a different outcome time. State the target and design, report uncertainty, and mark which parts depend on causal knowledge rather than on the observed table.

An effect is identifiable relative to data and a model class when every model consistent with those inputs gives the same value for it. Identification is conditional on assumptions; a precise association is not a substitute.
Agreement between one adjusted estimate and one trial estimate does not prove every causal assumption. A larger observational sample cannot by itself reveal a missing common cause.
Before computing, state why the available data and assumptions determine this particular intervention contrast.
Sample size addresses statistical precision for a chosen estimand. If an omitted common cause leaves multiple compatible intervention effects, observational precision does not choose one of them.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. Sample size addresses statistical precision for a chosen estimand. If an omitted common cause leaves multiple compatible intervention effects, observational precision does not choose one of them.
Sampling error and causal ambiguity are different problems.

A platform has a million coaching/passing records but omits an unmeasured factor that may cause both. No alternative identification design is supplied. What does the large sample establish about the coaching effect?
Sample size addresses statistical precision for a chosen estimand. If an omitted common cause leaves multiple compatible intervention effects, observational precision does not choose one of them.

Randomization supports the specified trial assignment contrast under its design conditions. Generalizing to different people, versions or timings requires a separate argument and usually additional evidence.

tables.label: Completed randomized assignment
tables.note: Assume random assignment, complete follow-up, consistent reminder versions and no interference. These are the study conditions, not a statement about other populations.

workbench.prompt: Final 4 of 4. A manager wants to apply the estimated +8-point reminder effect to a new population with a different reminder version and incomplete follow-up. Which assessment distinguishes identification, estimation and transport?
